coverage_notes: Exhaustive survey of canonical node-graph libraries (React Flow, Cytoscape.js, Sigma.js, AntV G6, Rete.js) across market, technical, and HCI dimensions. Coverage includes: (1) Official product pages and API documentation (T0/T1) for all five libraries; (2) Market sizing reports from Gartner, analyst firms, and data research vendors covering graph analytics (USD 2.5B+ market, 34% CAGR), graph databases (26.4% CAGR), knowledge graphs (15% CAGR), low-code platforms ($28.75B 2026 → $264.4B 2032, 32.2% CAGR), and data visualization tools (10.9% CAGR); (3) Comparative technical analysis (npm trends, architecture, layout engines, rendering technologies) from firstaimovers, cambridge-intelligence, and practitioner blogs; (4) HCI research on graph visualization accessibility, interaction design, and layout algorithms from arXiv, IEEE, Oxford Academic, and CMU HCII; (5) Performance benchmarks for WebGL vs Canvas vs SVG rendering; (6) Use-case studies (financial networks, supply chains, knowledge graphs, bioinformatics, LLM agents) from multiple sectors; (7) GitHub adoption metrics and maintainer funding models. Deduplication applied: 47 unique sources across 8 tiers. Notable coverage gaps: Gartner Magic Quadrant full PDFs are paywalled (reference-only); specific sales/revenue data for xyflow and other OSS maintainers not publicly available; deep-dive UX screencasts for all five libraries remain to be captured in ux_screens table. Named authorities: Tamara Munzner (visualization grammar), Shneiderman (interaction design), Gartner (market positioning), Neo4j (knowledge graphs), Cytoscape team (bioinformatics), xyflow/AntV/Linkurious (practitioners).
